title: El tiempo
goal: Talk about the weather, use querer and poder (stem-changing verbs), and make, accept and turn down invitations.

lessons.title: What's the weather like?
lessons.notes:
Spanish 'makes' most weather with **hacer**: **hace calor** (it's hot - literally 'it makes heat'), **hace frío**, **hace sol**, **hace viento**. Ask **¿Qué tiempo hace?**
Because calor, frío and sol are nouns, 'very' is **mucho**, not muy: **Hace mucho calor.**
Rain and snow have their own verbs: **llueve** (it's raining / it rains, from llover) and **nieva** (it snows). Clouds use estar: **Está nublado.**
**El tiempo** means both 'the weather' and 'time' - context tells you which.

sentences.en: It rains a lot in February.

sentences.es: Hace sol, vamos a la playa.
sentences.en: It's sunny, let's go to the beach.
accept_en: It's sunny, we're going to the beach.

sentences.en: The weather is good in spring.

accept_en: It is windy and it is cloudy.

sentences.es: Hace mal tiempo, voy a ver una película.
sentences.en: The weather is bad, I'm going to watch a film.
accept_en: The weather's bad, I'm going to watch a movie.

lessons.title: Querer and other e → ie verbs
lessons.notes:
Some verbs change their stem when it's stressed. In **querer** (to want) the **e** becomes **ie** - in every form except nosotros (and vosotros):
**quiero · quieres · quiere** · queremos · **quieren**
Draw a line round the changing forms in a table and it looks like a boot, so these are called 'boot verbs'. The endings stay regular.
Same pattern: **pensar** (pienso), **empezar** (empieza), **cerrar** (cierra), **preferir** (prefiero, prefieres).
**Querer + infinitive** = want to: **¿Quieres ir a la playa?** **Pienso que...** = I think that...

sentences.en: Do you want to go to the beach?
accept_en: Would you like to go to the beach?

sentences.en: We want to eat in a restaurant.
accept_en: We want to eat at a restaurant.

sentences.en: I think it's going to rain.
accept_en: I think that it's going to rain.

sentences.es: La clase empieza a las nueve.
La tienda cierra a las seis.

sentences.en: Do you prefer tea or coffee?
accept_en: Would you rather have tea or coffee?

sentences.en: I don't want to go out, it's cold.
What are you thinking of doing on Saturday?
accept_en: What do you plan to do on Saturday?
What are you planning to do on Saturday?

lessons.title: Poder and other o → ue verbs
lessons.notes:
The other big boot pattern turns **o** into **ue**. **Poder** (can, to be able to):
**puedo · puedes · puede** · podemos · **pueden**
Poder is followed straight by an infinitive: **¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?** (can I pay by card?) **No puedo ir** (I can't go).
Same pattern: **volver** (to come back: vuelvo), **dormir** (to sleep: duermo), and almorzar and jugar from earlier units.
The phrase every learner needs: **¿Puedes hablar más despacio, por favor?** (can you speak more slowly?) - with a stranger, **¿Puede...?**

sentences.en: Can you speak more slowly, please?
accept_en: Could you speak more slowly, please?
Can I pay with a card?
Can I pay by credit card?
I cannot go, I am sick.

sentences.en: We can go to the cinema tomorrow.
accept_en: We can go to the movies tomorrow.

sentences.es: Vuelvo a casa a las seis.
sentences.en: I come back home at six.
accept_en: I'll be back home at six.
I go back home at six.

sentences.en: What time are you coming back?
accept_en: What time do you get back?

sentences.es: No puedo dormir, hace mucho calor.
sentences.en: I can't sleep, it's very hot.
accept_en: I can't sleep, it's too hot.
I can't sleep, it's really hot.

lessons.title: Invitations
lessons.notes:
To invite: **¿Quieres...?** (do you want to...?) or the softer **¿Te gustaría...?** (would you like to...?). **¿Qué tal si...?** = how about...? - **¿Qué tal si vamos al cine?**
To accept: **¡Claro!**, **¡Qué buena idea!**, **¡Perfecto!**, **Me gustaría mucho.** To fix a time: **De acuerdo** (OK, agreed - Spain says **vale**).
To say no nicely: **Lo siento, no puedo**, then offer **otro día** or **la próxima vez**. **Quizás** = maybe.
'With me' and 'with you' are single words: **conmigo, contigo** (never 'con mí').

items.note: From venir (to come): vengo, vienes, viene.

sentences.en: Would you like to have dinner with me on Saturday?
accept_en: Would you like to have dinner with me on Saturday?

sentences.en: I'd like that a lot, thanks.
accept_en: I would like that very much, thank you.
I'm sorry, I can't. Some other day?

sentences.en: Are you coming to the party?
accept_en: Will you come to the party?

sentences.es: De acuerdo, nos vemos a las ocho.
accept: Vale, nos vemos a las ocho.
accept_en: All right, see you at eight.

sentences.es: Hace buen tiempo, ¿quieres ir a la playa?
sentences.en: The weather's nice, do you want to go to the beach?
accept_en: It's nice weather, do you want to go to the beach?

sentences.en: How about going to the cinema?
accept_en: How about we go to the movies?
Why don't we go to the cinema?
